requested.title: Path-based output withholding is bypassed with shell variable expansion

parsedVerdicts.reasoning: The local execution host invokes `sh -c <command>` with `process.env` (or a merge retaining it), so `$HOME` is expanded by the host shell and can resolve to the local user's home directory. The `bash` permission path calls `checkCommand`, but that guard only blocks selected Git/destructive operations and `.git` tokens; it does not impose a read scope or reject reads of `$HOME`. `filterLocalPayload` detects foreign access solely by matching literal `~`, `/Users`, `/home`, `/Volumes`, `/mnt`, or `/media` strings in the emitted tool-call and tool-result payloads. A command such as `cat "$HOME/.ssh/id_rsa"` contains none of those literal path forms, so its tool-call event does not populate `foreignCalls`. The resulting private-key content ordinarily contains no filesystem path either, so its tool-result preview also has a zero foreign-path count and is emitted instead of being replaced by `withheldOutput`. The event translator preserves the command and result under the same call ID, but this does not help because the map was never populated. Repository-supplied instruction files are delivered to the agent as data with a prompt-injection warning, but that is not an enforcement boundary against a malicious repository instruction influencing a locally initiated run. Git history shows the local-uplink feature was introduced in commit `123fcb9d`; the current `e0da16d0` change only rewrites its prose and does not add expansion-aware detection or filesystem confinement. Consequently, a prompt-injection-driven local shell read can place a local credential in project-visible `agent_run_events`, matching the finding's stated impact.
